name: Murtala Muhammed International Airport
before:
Nigeria's main international gateway, in Ikeja, Lagos State, and the base for Air Peace, the country's largest airline.

The layout is the thing to plan around. There is an international terminal and a domestic terminal about one kilometre apart, sharing the same runways. A client connecting between an international arrival and a domestic onward flight has to move between two separate buildings, so build proper time into the itinerary.

The international terminal was modelled on Amsterdam Schiphol and opened on 15 March 1979, built as part of a master plan meant to carry the airport through to the year 2000.

The airport was built during the Second World War and was originally called Lagos Airport. It was renamed in 1976 after Murtala Muhammed, the fourth head of state of Nigeria, following his assassination in a failed coup.
after:
Murtala Muhammed International is Lagos's international airport and the base for Air Peace.

International flights use the new terminal commissioned in March 2022: all airlines were moved into it by October 2023 so that the old terminal could be rebuilt. That reconstruction began in 2025 and is due to take 22 months, and a fire in the old terminal in February 2026 injured six people and briefly closed the airspace over Lagos.

Domestic flights use separate terminals, including MMA2, a privately run terminal opened in 2007, so allow time to change buildings on a connection between international and domestic flights.
